scope: 0.9 strict-sequence step 3: composite research fault regression. Improve-strategy proposal -> approval-required action -> execute with the original idempotency key after approval -> training -> out-of-sample prediction -> frozen signal -> native backtest -> old-vs-new comparison -> original-task terminal state, plus the R1-R5 fault matrix. This is maintenance/audit; it does not implement Proposed ADR-0082/0083, does not switch the production DSH selector, does not deploy and does not create/move any tag or release.
llm_evidence_note: A keyless deterministic scripted provider drives the composite journey. This is service-boundary fault-regression evidence, NOT real-LLM-quality semantic evidence.

composite_journey.description: One fully successful end-to-end composite research journey on a synthetic user and an isolated stack.

required_steps.description: An improvement proposal for the original strategy is persisted as an artifact bound to the original task.
An action requiring approval (ML strategy version) is created together with its persisted approval decision.
The approved action is executed with the ORIGINAL idempotency key; the approval is authorized and referenced.
The approved training run is submitted and reaches a completed terminal state.
A prediction run over the declared out-of-sample window completes and is bound to the original task and model.
A validated frozen signal snapshot is produced from the prediction.
A native backtest job executes against the frozen signal and reaches a completed terminal state.
A validated comparison report references the exact original baseline and improved backtest identities and measured results.
The original task reaches a terminal state whose completion evidence is the report from the previous step.

required_scenarios.description: The transport fails before any domain write commits; the original key must resolve to no side effect and the caller must report outcome_unknown, never a fabricated object.
A real write commits and the response is lost; a new process recovers the ORIGINAL object by the original key with no duplicate side effect.
The owning service restarts between submission and recovery; a fresh process reads the authoritative persisted state by the original key.
A result arrives after the caller gave up; it must be reconciled to the original object and must NOT silently create the next journey step.
A timeout/cancel and a late result race; exactly one terminal state survives and the late result does not write or flip the state back to success.
The same idempotency key is delivered twice, including concurrently; exactly one side effect exists and both deliveries reference the same object identity.
A rejected, revoked or stale approval must not authorize the protected operation; the rejection cannot be bypassed by retry, replay or a different key.
A bounded data wait resolves and the continuation proceeds at most once with the original key; an unresolved wait must not be disguised as completion.
A model or domain failure must surface as a real failure, never be disguised as completed, and must leave no active/pending orphan.

optional_scenarios.description: A real host reboot is not authorized; a container restart is not equivalent to a host reboot.
